speaker: Doctor
text: Please tell me exactly where on your leg it hurts when you walk, and have you noticed any swelling or redness in that area? Also, have you had any recent injuries or falls?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the pain is in the left knee but the limp suggests hip pathology, does the pain worsen when you lie on your left side at night? Also, has anyone noticed any stiffness in the morning or limited range of motion in that hip? I will need to perform a physical exam to check for limited internal rotation of the hip.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Synovitis of the Left Hip
